2) Routing: single model routing per tenant initially. We may want per-workspace overrides later but can start simple.
3) Request/response schema questions:
   - UI flow is chat-like (assistant + system messages) with occasional single-turn completions for snippets.
   - Tokenization: we estimate average user prompt size ~120 tokens, expected generation ~200 tokens max. Can you confirm how Redwood counts tokens for streaming responses vs final payload?
   - max_tokens: we want 256 hard cap on generations for chat responses.
   - stop sequences: we will use a custom stop token ("<END>") after structured JSON blocks.
   - streaming: preferred for the chat UI; we need to be able to render partial tokens server->client with websocket streaming. Is there a recommended strategy for safely assembling tokens + stop detection on the client?
4) Embeddings & reranker: we will store vectors in our own vector DB but want Redwood to return the full embeddings array in the response for offline debugging (not just scores).

I attached a short architecture note (alphaedge-arch-v1.pdf) showing where Redwood would sit in their stack. We can do Wed 10:30 PT for the deep-dive — Taylor and I will be there.

Sam — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. A few specific technical notes and a short checklist for the Wed deep-dive so we can be prescriptive during the call: 

A) Token accounting + streaming
- Redwood token accounting: we count tokens on the full request (system+history+prompt) and separately for generated tokens. For streaming responses we emit delta tokens as they are produced; the final billing uses total generated token count. If you need conservative upfront estimates for client-side caps, use generated_tokens_estimate = truncation_budget + safety_margin (we usually recommend +15%).
- Stop detection: we support user-supplied stop sequences. With streaming, clients should still buffer incoming chunks and apply a streaming-aware stop detector (check suffix of concatenated token stream against stop sequences). We have a small client helper in the SDK that does this reliably — I'll include the helper snippet on the call.

B) Chat vs completions recommendation
- For your chat-like UI use Chat APIs (structured messages: role + content). Chat supports assistant/system/message roles and preserves conversation state better for multi-turn contexts. Use completions only for isolated one-off snippet generation.
- For the POC, set max_tokens=256 on the call and server-side enforce a hard cut (we can enforce at the gateway to avoid runaway costs).

C) SDK & auth patterns
- Server-only API keys + short-lived per-session tokens for internal routing is our recommendation if you later add client features. For the POC server keys are fine.
- We recommend JWT-backed tenant claims to enable per-tenant routing in Redwood Dedicated if you evolve to multi-model routing later.

D) Embeddings
- We can return full embedding vectors if you set return_embeddings=true on the embeddings call. Note this increases bandwidth — consider returning top-k scores only in production, full arrays for debug runs.

Attachments: alphaedge-sample-payload.json (example chat request + embedding call) — I pasted a minimal example you can review on the call.
